text:
Cara: Quick question about a hire who starts as a contractor on 7/10 and converts to FT on 9/02. They want to know 3 things: 1) 401(k) eligibility and company match timing when payroll is split across contractor payroll and corporate payroll; 2) whether employer HSA contributions are pro-rated for month of conversion; 3) they have an old 403(b) from a previous employer  can they roll that into our 401(k) immediately or is there a waiting period.

Maya (People Ops): good scenario. Short answers up front: 1) match requires FT employee status + enrollment and is tied to the corporate payroll runs, so earliest match will be on the first corporate paycheck after enrollment and eligibility; contractor payroll doesn't transmit match. 2) HSA employer deposits follow our monthly schedule and are based on coverage tier on the 1st of the month, so conversion on 9/02 means the new deposit level starts 10/01 (no mid-month pro-rate by default). 3) inbound 403(b) rollovers depend on trustee rules; we allow inbound rollovers but recommend waiting until the 401(k) account is provisioned (usually after first payroll).

Cara: thanks. so payroll split means their pre-tax deferrals while on contractor payroll won't count for match later? They were planning to defer while contractor.

Devon - Benefits: correct. The contractor payroll is separate and doesn't feed our retirement plan recordkeeper. If you want match to apply to those dollars, they'd need to be paid on corporate payroll or we would have to grant a discretionary contribution after reconciliation (rare). Encourage manager to convert payroll before the pay period if match is required.

Cara: ok. what about partial month conversion and HSA catch-up for someone turning 55 during the conversion month?

Maya (People Ops): HSA catch-up (age 55+) is an employee election; payroll won't auto-enroll. If they turn 55 in September and want catch-up, submit the pre-tax election change in Workday before payroll cutoff for the pay you'd like to start withholding. Employer HSA deposit still follows monthly rule (1st of month snapshot) so employer amount won't retro pro-rate.

Payroll Bot: FYI: for conversion scenarios, Payroll needs HR rehire/employee record + effective date before cutoff to process benefits and deductions on the first corporate run. Off-cycle exceptions possible but require ticket + manager approval.

Devon - Benefits: 403(b) rollovers: yes we accept inbound rollovers; however if the previous plan is a 403(b) with employer contributions that have special restrictions, trustee may require additional paperwork. Also some 403(b) custodians only allow trustee-to-trustee transfers. Best practice: wait until the new 401(k) account is active (we see account IDs in our system) then initiate rollover with the prior custodian.

Cara: is there any limit on doing the rollover same day as first deferral? Manager wants it done quickly.

Devon - Benefits: no hard limit from our side, but operationally we avoid initiating rollovers until balances and payroll mapping have reconciled (usually 1-2 payrolls). Doing it same day can complicate reconciliation if there are timing differences; we can do it but will flag for manual review.

Cara: got it. action items?

Maya (People Ops): 1) schedule hire to be on corporate payroll for the first paycheck if match is important; 2) have employee submit Workday elections for HSA and 55+ catch-up before cutoff; 3) wait for 401(k) account provisioning then start inbound rollover. If you want help coordinating payroll cutoff windows, ping Payroll.

Cara: perfect, I'll coordinate with the hiring manager and loop payroll in. thanks! :thumbsup:
